item.title: Meta launches Waddle World, an AI‑powered pet journal app
item.description:
Meta launches Waddle World, an AI‑powered pet journal app

Meta has quietly released a new app called Waddle World, described as a tamagotchi‑style pet that chats with users and doubles as a daily journal.

🔍 Overview

  • Marketed as a “16‑bit pet care game” that is actually “a daily journal disguised as a pet.”
  • Features virtual creatures that chat with users and create doodles to illustrate conversations.

🧩 How it works

  • Users are encouraged to talk, not type, with their pets.
  • The app offers “cozy games” such as stacking groceries or word games.
  • The description emphasizes no pressure, no streaks, no scores – a warm little escape.

⚙️ Key features

  • Conversational virtual pet that generates doodles.
  • Daily‑journal functionality hidden behind pet‑care gameplay.
  • Free to download.
  • 16‑bit pixel‑art aesthetic (a “cozy 16‑bit world”).
  • “Cozy games” like grocery‑stacking and word puzzles.

🚀 Availability

  • Listed as free and only available to adults in the Philippines.
  • Meta also quietly launched an AI fashion app called Style Sketch, available only in Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand.
  • Meta has not confirmed whether either app will appear in the United States or other markets.

💡 Why it matters

  • The launch aligns with Meta’s broader push of a sweet mascot and small Charm gadgets for its Muse AI agent, indicating a focus on light‑hearted, conversational AI experiences.
App Region(s) where listed
Waddle World Philippines (adults only)
Style Sketch Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand

#Meta #AI #PetJournal #ChatBots

Source: Meta quietly launched an ‘AI pet journal’ app

item.title: States Pass Industry-Backed Laws Regulating AI Chatbot Companions
item.description:
States Pass Industry-Backed Laws Regulating AI Chatbot Companions

Legislators in multiple U.S. states have enacted new laws that set basic safety standards for AI chatbots, but the measures are largely shaped by industry influence.

🔍 Overview

Lawmakers are passing industry‑backed bills to guard against the worst outcomes, rather than addressing more common problems.

🏛️ Legislative Landscape

  • This year, for example, Google backed bills to regulate AI chatbots in several states.
  • The legislation mandated basic protections against sexual content and promotion of self‑harm that tech companies should have established regardless, but with broad carve‑outs that could exempt some of the most popular services.
  • Passing these bills allowed legislators to claim a safety win while efforts to promote stronger legislation—laws designed to prevent children from becoming emotionally dependent on AI—failed.
  • This playbook worked in states like Nebraska, producing legislation heavily influenced by industry at the expense of bills that would have done more to hold companies accountable.
  • Sam Hiner is the cofounder and executive director of the Young People’s Alliance, where he coordinated a coalition of advocates to pass laws regulating AI companions in eight states in 2026—laws such as California’s SB1119.

🤖 Industry Response

  • An AI company promises that its chatbot will not encourage suicide.
  • But companies can clear these low bars while continuing to make products that leave young people dependent on simulated friendships or trapped in feeds built to keep them scrolling.

👶 Youth Impact

  • A third of teens now choose to discuss serious matters with AI companions instead of other people.
  • MIT researchers found that young people using ChatGPT to write essays showed weaker brain connectivity during the task, and their evidence indicated that “cognitive debt” persisted even after the task was complete.
  • Companies should be prohibited from designing companions that pretend to be conscious or profess love to users, and they should face independent scrutiny of how their systems affect relationships and people’s ability to think for themselves.

📚 Calls for Stronger Action

  • Technology companies and school districts should have to show beyond a reasonable doubt that AI improves learning and critical thinking before making it a fixture in classrooms.
  • We should demand safety as a minimum, yes—and then demand considerably more.
  • The companies that have inserted their products into nearly every part of modern life have earned obligations far greater than avoiding the next terrible headline.

❓ What Remains Unknown

  • There is plenty we still need to learn about the long‑term effects.
  • We already have reason to ask whether technology marketed as making us more capable is eroding the habits and relationships that help us develop capabilities in the first place.

#AIRegulation #Chatbots #YouthSafety #AICompanions

Source: The focus on AI safety disasters ignores everyday harms

item.title: Danish Survey Finds No Wage or Hour Impact from AI Chatbot Adoption
item.description:
Danish Survey Finds No Wage or Hour Impact from AI Chatbot Adoption

A large‑scale Danish study of 25,000 workers in 11 AI‑exposed occupations finds that using generative AI chatbots did not change earnings or hours worked.

🔍 Overview

  • The research links survey responses to monthly administrative records through December 2024.
  • It compares chatbot users with comparable non‑users in the same occupations and workplaces.

📊 Survey Design

  • Two representative surveys were fielded with Statistics Denmark in late 2023 and late 2024.
  • Each round invited 115,000 workers; the 2024 round yielded about 25,000 valid responses from 7,000 workplaces.
  • Respondents were drawn from registers, allowing linkage to earnings, hours, and occupation data for both respondents and roughly 3 million other Danish workers.
  • The sample matches the workforce on age, gender, experience, earnings, and wealth.

🛠️ Occupations Studied

Occupation Exposure
Software developers High
IT support specialists High
Customer support specialists High
Office clerks High
Accountants High
Financial advisors High
HR professionals High
Legal professionals High
Marketing professionals High
Journalists High
Teachers High

📈 Findings

  • Headline result: a precise null – no measurable effect on earnings or hours for either chatbot‑using workers or firms that adopt chatbots.
  • 43 % of workers reported that their employer explicitly encourages chatbot use.
  • Policies reported in the 2024 survey were: encouraged, allowed, not allowed, no policy, or unknown.

💡 Why it matters

  • Earlier work (Brynjolfsson, Chandar, & Chen 2025) documented sharp drops in early‑career employment in AI‑exposed occupations, raising concerns about displacement.
  • Denmark’s rapid generative‑AI uptake—on par with the United States—provides a clean window to test those concerns, and the null finding suggests that, at least through December 2024, chatbot adoption has not translated into wage or hour reductions.

#AI #LaborMarket #Denmark #Chatbots

Source: Still waters, rapid currents: Early labor market transformation under generative AI | Brookings
